decisions.reason: Published October 7, within the September 16–October 15 UTC window. Useful new computational case study: the authors report three 24-experiment campaigns with frozen evaluation and one-hour training budgets per trial, not per campaign ([saved text, §§2–3, Table 1](data/assets/a007976d7a6dcb8c99635a7e/22bcded05aecba83c6a4594604bdc843c3061c7ccdf19d4be43c9ea27beaec4f/text.txt)). Accept as preprint evidence for bounded delegation and hardware-sensitive results, not general superiority. Only Loop B receives held-out testing; single-seed trials, model–hardware confounding, unmatched reference compute and no declared-space tuner comparison limit inference (§3.2; §4). Examine the numerical inconsistency: Table 3 gives 0.836 versus 0.833, a displayed difference of 0.003, while the prose says 0.002; do not repeat that delta as resolved. Small retained gains lack estimated run variance (§3.1). The repository is linked in the abstract, but its execution artifacts are not supplied or independently verified here. No independent replication or external researcher assessment is supplied; no conflict disclosure appears in the supplied text, so commercial interests remain unknown. Student implication: freeze the evaluator, budget the whole search and replicate retained changes before treating them as defaults.

September 29 publication is in-window. Accept narrowly as a physical-laboratory practitioner contrast: founders describe furnace instability, telemetry and replicates ([saved transcript, s00308–s00373, 877.58–1005.08 seconds](data/assets/ade5c65097bf35b3d1cb467e/5a82503b8b0e7e873cc96ddaa5b89b9957e647009d50cff4f549b940594dfeef/segments.json)), and recording hypotheses, predictions and execution lineage (s00849–s00875, 2040.8–2099.88). These concrete accounts support discussion of what students should log; they do not demonstrate measured agent reliability. The sample-holder correction is an undated, self-reported anecdote without inspectable logs or controls (s00890–s00908, 2131.44–2178.56). Novelty is the recent account, not a dated experimental breakthrough. Do not adopt the introduction's thousands-per-day capability claim: later discussion describes that scale as a future goal (s00023–s00024 versus s00747–s00750). Cost reductions likewise lack workload, accuracy and hardware comparisons (s01100–s01116, 2613–2652.46). Commercial interests are explicit in customer systems and retained IP (s01206–s01223, 2848.96–2894.64); the two founders and any other founder interview cannot independently corroborate these claims. No external replication or independent laboratory assessment is supplied. Transcript wording remains provisional; exclude unsupported performance and superintelligence claims.

October 5 publication is in-window and the workspace-preserving context reset is directly relevant to student experiment design. However, defer this version until supporting artifacts and reporting inconsistencies are resolved. The headline 66.0% and 44.4% improvements concern min–max normalized aggregate scores, not universal task gains; LWE-rec favors the single-run baseline ([saved text, Table 1 and §5.2](data/assets/b1f8d59a9e19a86e11b1f913/d65818cf27d705500dbc6ee16a00aa24ff79c55f10cb82e034d39e559cbc1994/text.txt)). Section 5.1 says every run uses the 33%/66% cadence and five replicates, whereas Appendix G includes 50% rounds and Appendix B specifies four tinyCIFAR seeds. Appendix A's Borden-inv means differ from Table 1 without a clear reconciliation. Appendix I labels prompts but omits their actual text; no accessible study-code or run-log link is supplied. Equal token-credit budgets do not establish equal total execution cost: Appendix B explicitly distinguishes credits from wall-clock and includes GPU training without sufficient hardware accounting. The embedding's held-out agreement tests the same model's similarity judgments, not independent scientific validation (§3; Appendix F). The work was conducted at Microsoft Research and evaluates GitHub Copilot CLI, an institutional commercial connection to disclose (§1 footnote; §2; acknowledgments). No independent replication is supplied. Potential novelty is inference-time search control, explicitly without weight updates (§7), but the present evidence cannot support a reproducible performance recommendation.

September 23 UTC publication is in-window. Accept as researcher guidance on inspectable workflows, not evidence of autonomous-agent performance. Concrete advice covers planning preregistration, sharing code and variable definitions, and allowing time for methodological review ([saved transcript, s00753–s00764, 2357.07–2387.75; s00795–s00811, 2460.23–2498.03; s01090–s01104, 3276.07–3314.07 seconds](data/assets/e351f88c9bbc63c033f1aab7/de7f1e6f75069d6e82b0732ba9729ef01809dd0621fa585ccb3cb1690c97dcc9/segments.json)). Editorial inference: these practices help students make agent-assisted experiments reviewable. Novelty is the recent discussion, not a new measured method: the report was presented in June, and September publication is only anticipated in the recording (s00055–s00059; s00568–s00570). Its full text and the cited survey are not supplied, so neither can establish findings here. Preserve the correction that authors still matter (s00313–s00317; s00344–s00348). The earlier 'not time-consuming' encouragement must be qualified by later explicit extra-time advice (s00747–s00757 versus s01076–s01104). Automatic transcription is provisional; ambiguous wording cannot establish a contradictory position without audio review. Disclose the first guest's report authorship and training role, and the second guest's journal editorship when discussing their recommendations (s00055–s00059; s00390–s00393; s00650–s00653). These are involved researcher perspectives, not independent validation of the accepted agent studies; no controlled outcome evaluation is supplied.
